claims.evidence: Photo 1 clearly shows the model name 'NV180' printed on the body.
Photo 1 shows a digital screen and an attached embroidery unit.

risks.risk: Internal mechanical timing or motor failure under load.
risks.proof: A video clip of the machine completing a full embroidery pattern and a straight stitch on fabric.
risks.if_unproven: as requiring a professional service and timing adjustment.

risks.risk: Missing essential accessories like embroidery hoops and the foot controller.
risks.proof: A photo of all included accessories laid out (hoops, feet, power cable, and pedal).
risks.if_unproven: as missing all accessories, requiring separate purchase of hoops and controller.

risks.risk: Touch screen digitizer failure or dead zones.
risks.proof: A video showing a user selecting different patterns on the touch screen.
risks.if_unproven: as having a partially non-functional interface.

proof_requests: Video of the machine in operation (sewing and embroidery).
Photo of the embroidery hoops, foot controller, and power cable.
Photo of the accessory tray contents (presser feet, bobbins).
response.reason: The witness has clearly identified the model as a Brother NV180 and confirmed it powers on. While the seller misnamed the model, the physical evidence allows for a worst-case valuation.
